resolutions.researcher_notes: FERC's own Notice of Availability of the Draft Environmental Impact Statement for the Gulf Crossing Project (Federal Register, publisher: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Docket Nos. CP07-398-001/CP07-401-000) states the project consists of 'Approximately 353.2 miles of 42-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline extending east-southeast from Grayson County, Texas and Bryan County, Oklahoma to Madison Parish, Louisiana' -- an exact match (353.2 rounds to the sheet's 353.00 mi). This is a single publisher, so tier is medium/independent false rather than high. For context (not proposed as refs, since they describe a materially different figure/stage and would not tightly support the exact 353.00 value): Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' own SEC 10-Ks describe a slightly larger as-designed/as-built mileage for the same pipeline -- 355 mi (FY2006, initial project announcement), 357 mi (FY2007 and FY2008/2009, as constructed) -- and Gulf Crossing's own company website (Wayback capture of gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx, 2019) and Boardwalk's FY2018 10-K both later describe the system as approximately 375 miles. Read together these look like normal growth from the original 2007 FERC-filed mainline mileage (353.2 mi, matching the sheet) to a later as-built figure inclusive of loops/laterals added after the FERC EIS (356.3 mi mainline + 17.8 mi loop per FERC's March 2008 Final EIS notice, E8-6315) to an even later 'system' total (357-375 mi) as compression/looping was added over the 2009-2019 period. None of this contradicts the sheet's 353.00 mi as the originally-proposed/certificated mainline length; it just means later company disclosures describe the grown system rather than the original filed mileage, so I did not force them in as a second independent source for the SAME 353.00 figure.

Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2008 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2009-02; automated substring screen failed on my literal search label but I fetched and grepped the document directly and confirmed the exact sentence) states: 'Gulf Crossing's supply sources are mainly unconventional gas sources in the Barnett Shale and Caney Woodford Shale' -- an exact match to the sheet's 'Barnett Shale, Texas; Caney/Woodford Shale, Oklahoma.' The Wayback capture of Gulf Crossing's own company page (gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx, 2019-07-26 snapshot) independently repeats: Gulf Crossing 'provides takeaway capacity from the Barnett Shale in Texas and the Caney/Woodford Shale in Oklahoma.' I am NOT marking this independent -- both documents originate from the same corporate family (Boardwalk Pipeline Partners / its wholly-owned subsidiary Gulf Crossing describing itself), which the brief's independence rule treats as one origin (an applicant's own filing and its own website are the company's own self-description, not two distinct publishers), so tier is medium rather than high. I checked FERC's Federal Register notices (Draft/Final EIS notices, notice of application, notice of intent) for independent third-party language naming the Barnett Shale / Caney-Woodford Shale specifically -- these are short procedural notices and none contain that language (the full underlying EIS document, which likely does discuss gas supply basins, is not accessible as plain text via the Federal Register API). Natural Gas Intel's 'Gulf Crossing Pipeline Open for Business' article (a seed citation, a genuinely distinct trade-press publisher) is a soft-redirect dead end -- the live URL now serves an unrelated 2026 story, and no Wayback snapshot exists for that path (checked via both the wayback/available API and the CDX API, both returned empty), so I could not recover it as a second independent publisher.

CONCERN: I could not find any source stating a $121,000,000 cost for the Gulf Crossing Pipeline, and every capital-cost figure I did find for this project is roughly 10-15x higher. Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2006 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2007), announcing the project, put the *combined* cost of Gulf Crossing plus its associated Gulf South/Fayetteville-Greenville expansions at 'approximately $3.3 billion' for 2007-2009. The FY2008 10-K (filed 2009) itemizes Gulf Crossing separately in its capital-projects table: 'Gulf Crossing Project -- Estimated Total Cost $1,800 [million] -- Cash Invested through December 31, 2008 $1,403.5 [million].' That is consistent with the physical scope (approximately 357 miles of new 42-inch interstate transmission pipeline plus compression, a very large-diameter, long-haul project) -- $121 million would imply roughly $340,000 per mile of 42-inch pipe including compression, which is implausibly low for a 2007-2009-vintage 42-inch interstate line (steel/labor costs were unusually high in that period, which the 10-Ks themselves flag as a cost driver). I searched SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Gulf Crossing' plus '121' / '121,000,000' / '$121 million' and reviewed the FY2006, FY2007, FY2008, and FY2009 Boardwalk 10-Ks directly (all fetched and grepped) -- none contains a $121 million figure tied to Gulf Crossing; the closest analogous number is Boardwalk's Southeast Expansion project (a different, smaller project) at $775 million estimated cost, still far above $121 million. I also checked whether $121 million could be a partial transaction value (e.g., proceeds from Boardwalk's disclosed but apparently unconsummated plan to sell a 49% interest in Gulf Crossing to a third party) -- the 10-Ks mention that structure only in the context of the $3.3 billion aggregate figure and never state a dollar value for the 49% stake itself. WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session (both at the start and again on a later retry) so I could not run open web searches for a possible EIA/trade-press citation of $121 million; everything above came from direct API/document fetches (Federal Register API, SEC EDGAR full-text search, and the four Boardwalk 10-Ks fetched by URL). Given the sheet's own likely source population (other Boardwalk-family pipelines in this cohort, e.g. Tiger and Corpus Christi/Cheniere, show similar single-figure SegmentCost fields that sometimes don't match audited totals), this reads as a probable data-entry or unit/scope error on the sheet -- flagging for Update rather than changing the value or fabricating a citation for it.
